name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>: domain=dialog_sprite, descriptor=blit_mirrored. Accurately reflects purpose (opaque dialog-pixel sprite painter that writes a horizontally mirrored image by walking dst LEFT/DEC EDI per decoded pixel). No Ghidra address residue. Verified against decomp, disassembly (MOV [EDI],AL; DEC EDI distinguishes it from the normal sibling's STOSB) and caller fd2_paint_portrait_to_dialog_area.
purpose: Opaque dialog-portrait sprite painter that draws a horizontally mirrored (right-to-left) image: same dialog-pixel decoder/header layout as fd2_dialog_sprite_blit_normal, but dst is the row's RIGHT edge and each decoded pixel walks LEFT.
logic_summary: width=hdr[+0], row_count=hdr[+2], cursor=hdr+4, state=0 seeded once and threaded across the whole rectangle. Per row: dst_row=dst (right edge), col=width; per pixel: state=fd2_decode_dialog_pixel_byte(state,&cursor); *dst_row=(uint8)state; dst_row-- (mirror walk left). After each row: dst+=stride; row_count--. Post-test do/while on both loops. Differs from the normal sibling @0x4E8AF only in the per-pixel step (DEC EDI vs INC via STOSB); row-to-row step (saved row-start via PUSH/POP EDI then +stride) is identical, so the image flips horizontally only. Inner loop count is the literal width header word (LOOP with CX=BP, ECX pre-zeroed); the decompiler's 'while (extraout_ECX != 1)' is a phantom from the LOOP/CALL interaction.
signature: void fd2_dialog_sprite_blit_mirrored(uint32 dst, uint32 sprite_hdr, uint32 stride)
